**Andrew here.** We’re getting ready for our annual DealBook Summit on Wednesday. The past week has brought an avalanche of news, and you’ve sent us some extraordinary questions for our onstage interviewees, including Vice President **JD Vance** , Prime Minister **Mark Carney** of Canada, **Elon Musk** of SpaceX, **Sam Altman** of OpenAI, **Christine Lagarde** of the European Central Bank, **Satya Nadella** of Microsoft, the entrepreneur **Hailey Bieber** and many more.


We’ll have a special edition of DealBook tomorrow morning with information about how you can follow along all day. Now onto today’s news.


## Nvidia’s next big test


Stock markets appear poised for more losses as the artificial intelligence sector, and Nvidia in particular, continued to weigh on investors.


The chipmaker is facing its latest crucible since the resignation last week of its leader, **Jensen Huang** : quarterly earnings. They will underscore the debut of **Colette Kress** ’s era as interim C.E.O., with analysts ready to pepper her with questions about the health and future of the chipmaker, including whether her old boss might seek a comeback and whether she’ll turn off the investment spigot.


**The latest:**


-


Nvidia shares are up in premarket trading. The company’s stock has declined 27 percent since late October, wiping out over $1 trillion in market value.


-


Nvidia’s performance last quarter isn’t what investors are worried about. Analysts expect the company, whose chips power most of the A.I. boom, to have nearly doubled revenue, to $109 billion.


**Analysts want to know what lies ahead for Nvidia.** That includes the true state of its China business amid questions about Huang’s affair with **Alice Huang** , an executive at a data center company accused of smuggling Nvidia chips to China and who U.S. intelligence agencies believe was a Chinese asset. (On Monday, the Trump administration moved to block China from gaining access to Nvidia chips[via data centers](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/16/us/politics/trump-china-ai-chip-loophole.html) based outside its borders.)


They will also want to know about efforts to find a permanent replacement for Huang, particularly as a “who’s who” list of Silicon Valley seeks to restore the former Nvidia chief to his position. Also potentially in favor of such a move: **President Trump** , who told reporters on Monday, “[I would not mind that](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/16/us/politics/trump-jensen-huang-nvidia.html) .”


-


Nvidia’s board isn’t considering bringing Huang back as C.E.O., DealBook hears. That said, the three leading candidates for the job, based on[trading on Kalshi](https://kalshi.com/markets/kxnvdaceo/next-nvidia-ceo/kxnvdaceo-29jan) , are **Rene Haas** , the C.E.O. of the chip designer Arm; **Ian Buck** , a top technical executive at Nvidia; and Huang himself.


Some analysts may also ask about the solidity of Nvidia’s chip sales after Huang’s departure, particularly after **Elon Musk** , a major customer, warned publicly that “at least some of those critical deals[will be lost](https://x.com/elonmusk/status/2121613402846204253) .”
